name: Kyle Daukaus
event: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott
summary: Philadelphia submission specialist (17-5, 1 NC; 4-5, 1 NC UFC), the 'D'arce Knight', who returned to the UFC in 2025 with two sub-minute finishes (Michel Pereira KO 0:43, Gerald Meerschaert d'arce 0:50) before Bo Nickal stopped him in the first round at UFC Freedom 250 in June. Elite front-headlock and choke game; his chin against power strikers is the issue.

how_they_fight.Striking: Long straight left (it dropped Meerschaert seconds in) and improved striking since his regional run, but not a volume striker (about 3.5 a minute) and hittable (about 51% defense). Two career KO/TKO wins, both in round one.
how_they_fight.Grappling: The weapon: 12 career submissions, d'arce and front-headlock chokes a specialty. He hunts chokes off scrambles and off opponents' shots. Took Jamie Pickett down three times and finished him at 4:59 of R1; choked out Kevin Holland in 2021 after an accidental clash of heads (ruled a no contest).
how_they_fight.Defense: Stopped three times, all by strikes: Roman Dolidze (R1, 1:13), Eryk Anders (R2) and Bo Nickal (R1, 4:34; taken down, cut with an elbow, then dropped by a right hook). UFC.com notes he has struggled with fighters who close distance fast and create chaos, though he has looked more composed lately.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Can go three rounds (decision win over Stoltzfus, decision losses to Brendan Allen and Phil Hawes), but his finishes are early-to-middle: 8 of 14 stoppage wins in R1, 4 in R2, 2 in R3. All three of his stoppage losses came in R1-R2.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Patient and opportunistic: waits for an opponent to shoot or get hurt, then jumps on the neck. Fights well when ahead; less sure when pressured.

patterns: Early finisher: 8 of 14 stoppage wins in round 1 (both UFC 2025 finishes inside 60 seconds)
Front headlock / d'arce off scrambles and opponents' takedown attempts
Straight left to hurt, then jumps on the finish
All three stoppage losses by strikes in rounds 1-2 (Dolidze, Anders, Nickal)
concerns: Durability against heavy hitters coming forward
Off a first-round TKO loss in June
Withdrew from a booked UFC 327 bout with Vicente Luque before being moved to the White House card (reason not reported)
keys_to_beat: Pressure him and make the exchanges chaotic early
Don't shoot lazy takedowns into his front headlock
Keep it standing and land power shots in the pocket

news.text: Booked against Marc-Andre Barriault at middleweight in Edmonton, off his June loss to Bo Nickal.
Said he was taken off his UFC 327 fight with Vicente Luque and moved to the White House card to face Bo Nickal.
